THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
These are appeals filed by the claimants aggrieved by the dismissal order passed in MVC No.77/2008 and MVC No.78/2008, dated 20.04.2012.
MVC No.77/2008 was filed by the pillion rider against the dismissal of the same MFA No.9839/2012 is filed.
MVC No.78/2012 was filed by the rider against the dismissal of the same he has filed MFA No.9841/2012.

MVC No.77/2008 filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.11,65,000/- and MVC No.78/2008 is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.9,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimants in the road traffic accident.

It is the case of the claimants that on 07.07.2010 both the claimants after having coffee with an intention to go to their native place Matadadoddi village was going in front of Iyengar V.B.Bakery,
Mandya Malavalli main road towards Halagur road in their Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle and when the rider of the vehicle was riding the same carefully and cautiously at about 3.30 p.m.

At that time one Hero Honda Splendor motorcycle bearing No.KA-11/R-2859 has been driven NC:
2023:KHC:37682 by its driver in a rash and negligent manner came from Malavalli side and dashed against the motorcycle driven by the claimant.
Due to the said impact both the rider and the pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident the claimants were shifted to K.M.Doddi Hospital.
On the same day the complaint was given by the pillion rider mentioning the vehicle number as KA-11/J-1890.
Thereafter on the next day according to the claimant it is mistakenly mentioned and they have given the number of vehicle number as KA-11/R-2859.
Basing on the additional statement the police have filed the charge-sheet against the driver of the said vehicle.
It is stated that before the Court below he accepted his guilt and paid fine.
3. The Insurance Company had filed the written- statement and they have disputed the involvement of the vehicle insured by them.
It is their case that when initially the complaint is given mentioning one number, later for the purpose of claiming the compensation the vehicle is implicated in this case.
The Court below on this issue had discussed and gave findings that the involvement of the vehicle cannot be disbelieved.

The claimants have come to the Court with unclean NC:
2023:KHC:37682 hands.
The Court below had observed that according to him he had given further statement before the police on the same day mentioning the correct number of the vehicle.

The Court below also examined the evidence of RW3 who is the police constable and stated that further statement was given to RW3 and the same was recorded by RW3, whereas RW3 deposed that at the time of recording mahazar witnesses stated about different motorcycle number.
Accordingly, he recorded further statement of PW1.

The Court below had observed that in this spot mahazar, Ex.P2,
Ex.P3 seizure mahazar, there was no mention about the same.
The Court below had observed if RW3 came to know about the different motorcycle number he would have made a note in the said mahazar itself.
RW3 admitted that in the mahazar available there is no such reference about different motorcycle number.
The Court below had also observed about the discrepancy with regard to the dates.
According to PW1 it was recorded on 07.07.2007 whereas Ex.R8 is dated 08.07.2007.

The Court below had also considered the evidence of PW2 who is an eye-witness in that regard the Court below had observed that he is working as SDA in a school and his school timings is from 10.00 a., to 4.30 NC: 2023:KHC:37682 p.m, on that day it was Saturday, it is also elicited that to reach his village Alabhujanahalli there is no reason for him to go through the spot near where the accident had taken place.
The Court below had stated the presence of PW2 at the place of occurrence.
Further swhen PW1 was very much acquainted with RW3 when he is very much available at the accident spot.
He had accompanied them to the hospital.
But as per the evidence it is one K.B.Boregowda who was taken the claimants to the hospital.

4. The Court below had observed that itself shows that PW2 not at all present at that time and whole story is created by PW1 and PW3 by colluding with the concerned police and further as per the IMV report the vehicle in which the claimants were traveling was damaged and there is no damage to the other vehicle.

On this aspect also the Court below had disbelieved the case of the claimants and observed that the claimants have not approached the Court with clean hands and dismissed the M S Suresh vs Shivaswamy J on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158839495/
4 claim petition.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that the Court below without considering the evidence NC: 2023:KHC:37682 on record and the circumstances had dismissed the claim petition.
According to the learned counsel as the claimant had met with an accident and he was in a shock and he had taken treatment under that effect.
He had mentioned the number of the vehicle wrongly and immediately on the second day he had given the additional statement to the police mentioning the vehicle number.
He submits that just because the other vehicle was not damaged that cannot be a ground for the Court to come to the conclusion that the said vehicle is not involved.
He submits that at all times it is not necessary that the offending vehicle should also be damaged.

Learned counsel submits that the Tribunal in a very hyper technical manner without considering the evidence had dismissed the petition.
6.

On the other hand learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the Court below rightly considering the discrepancies in the evidence of PW1 and RW3 and Ex.R8 had rightly dismissed the claim petition and the claimants have implicated the said vehicle only for the purpose of claiming the compensation.
Having heard learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
As per the claimant initially the vehicle number is mentioned as KA-11/J-1890.

Thereafter according to him the accident had taken place on 07.07.2007 and on the next day on 08.07.2007, he had given additional statement basing on that the police have registered the case against the other vehicle i.e.,
KA-11/R-2859 and the charge-sheet was filed and also the driver of the vehicle had accepted the guilt and paid the fine.
The Claimant had taken different stands and his evidence cannot be considered for the reason.
In the petition it is stated that on the second day i.e., on 08.07.2007 he went and gave the additional statement.
When it comes to his evidence he states that on the same day he had given additional statement and that was recorded by RW3.

When it comes to the evidence of RW3, RW3 gives altogether a different picture where he says that while they were conducting the panchanama the witnesses stated about this number and he also admits the fact that such numbers was not mentioned in the panchanama.

All these circumstances literally proves that the claim made by the claimants are not genuine and for the purpose of claiming the compensation,
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:37682 they have changed the statement and mentioned the number of the vehicle.
In that view of the matter, the Court below had rightly considered all these aspects and dismissed the claim petition.
This Court finds no reasons to interfere with.
8. Accordingly, both the appeals of the claimants are dismissed.
i) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
